{"design":"PLAN (2026-11-02, awaiting Mark). protocol-06 §5.7 L2206-2337.

Inbound (follower side, the provider of the target/requester user):
- Routes POST /v1/requestConsent/{targetDomain} and /v1/updateConsent/{requesterDomain} (decision .5.16 domain placeholders); directory lists both again (back out of .6.78's omission); directory_routes test then covers them.
- Logic in follower/consent.rs: decode ConsentEntry strictly (existing mimi-protocol type, decisions .5.68/.5.69), then check:
  requestConsent: op is request or cancel; targetUri domain = this provider; requesterUri domain = From domain; path targetDomain = this provider.
  updateConsent: op is grant or revoke; requesterUri domain = this provider; targetUri domain = From domain; path requesterDomain = this provider.
  From is a consistency check only (decision .6.9).
- Effect in v1: none stored, nothing changes consent::allows (decision .7.9 implicit allow, .21 no enforcement). grant clientKeyPackages are decoded (untrusted input, size caps from the type) and dropped, not added to any group. Log at debug, never bodies at INFO.
- Responses: 201 empty on accept, for known and unknown users alike (§5.7 allows 201 to avoid revealing existence); 400 for undecodable body, wrong operation for the endpoint, domain mismatch, or bad From.

Outbound: PeerClient::request_consent / update_consent (Endpoint variants with variables targetDomain / requesterDomain), expecting 201 like notify; NotOffered if the peer omits them. No caller in v1 (no JMAP surface, .7.9); used by tests and the interop harness.

Tests (regression first, independent oracles): Haven-encoded fixtures already committed (tests/fixtures/haven consent_request.bin, consent_grant.bin) posted to the routes -> 201; the same bytes with the operation byte swapped (hand-edited, byte offset commented) -> 400; domain-mismatch and bad-From cases -> 400; outbound against a local axum server asserting path, From and exact body, and a non-201 -> Rejected.

Decisions to record: D1 inbound effect = accept and drop (v1); D2 201 for unknown users (no existence oracle); D3 400 for operation/domain violations (§5.7 says 'needs to be' but names no status; INVENTED status choice). Docs: Limitations in follower/consent.rs, http.rs, peer.rs."}
